service.description: The identities the user may send as: each identity of an account the user may send from ({value identity:id or account:id, label, emailAccountId, emailIdentityId, emailAddress, displayName, accountName, signatureHtml, signaturePlacementEnumId, useForReplies, isDefault}), then the Internal identity (value internal: an internal message as the user). defaultValue is the default identity of MAIL_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT when that account is one the user may send from, else the default identity of the first account, else internal.

What the composer starts with. A draft (emailMessageId, one the user may send from): its identity, recipients, subject, body (its quoted part apart), attachments and the message it answers. A reply (replyToEmailMessageId, a message the user reads; replyAll for every recipient but the user) or a forward (forwardEmailMessageId: a draft made now, with copies of the files): the account it came to, the sender (its Reply-To) and recipients, "Re:" or "Fwd:" and the quoted message. An internal reply (replyToCommEventId of a Message or Comment the user sees; replyToSender for the sender only, off the mailbox) or a Chatter "Reply by email" (replyToCommEventId of an email on the record recordEntity, recordId, which the user must see): the internal thread's recipients, which reply#CommunicationEvent keeps, or the email's. A new message takes to, cc, bcc, subject and body (mailto style), contactListId (a post to that mailbox), and the record chip recordEntity, recordId. Each recipient is {value, label, kind (address, party or mailbox), locked}.

The recipients the To, Cc and Bcc chips offer for the term: for email (mode email), the email addresses of the parties the user may see (the directory under the Comms app's entity filters, so another organization's parties stay out, and the user's own personal contacts, R7: name or address), the contact groups of the books the user may see (a group chip expands to its members on send), and the addresses of the user's recent mail; for an internal message (mode internal), the users (by name or user name) and the mailboxes the user may post to. Options {value, label, kind}: value is the address as a header ("Name" <address>), party:id, group:id or list:id.

The call-context provider of IronStone's Comms root (plans/archive/Comms-Framework.md §3.3, V5: the screen pop of an inbound phone call, in the ring bar and the call): the parties whose telecom number is the caller's (number, E.164), among those the user may see (read with authorization on: call#Providers runs this as the Comms app, so its entity filters keep another organization's parties out, as in get#RecipientSource; a private contact only for its owner), each with a link to the contact; and their open requests (cases: not completed or cancelled), with links. At most 5 contacts and 10 records.

The call-target provider of IronStone's Comms root (plans/archive/Comms-Framework.md §3.3, the hardening pass): of the users in userIdList, those the signed-in user may not call, transfer a call to or add to a call. A user may be reached when their party is one the user may see, under the same rules as get#RecipientSource: read with authorization on, so the Comms app's entity filters (MANTLE_USER_ORG's organizations) keep another organization's people out, not disabled, and not another user's private contact. A user with no party belongs to no organization (a system or service account), so no organization is kept from them: they may be reached, as without this provider. Everyone is refused when no one is signed in.

The recipient-source provider of IronStone's Comms root (plans/archive/Comms-Framework.md §3.3, V3: the Dialer's search): the people and organizations the user may see (the directory under the Comms app's entity filters, so another organization's parties stay out, and their own personal contacts and contact books' parties, R7: privateOwnerUserId empty or theirs) whose name or phone number matches text, with their phone numbers (Mantle telecom contact mechs, made E.164 by the deployment's rules) and each number's purpose. kinds: phone (or empty) asks for numbers; a call for other kinds alone answers nothing here. Each recipient {itemId (party:id), kind (person or organization), name, phoneList [{number, label}]}; at most limit (25), its own page. Authority is the signed-in user's: a private contact of another user is never answered.

The chips of a recipient field ([{value, label}] or their JSON) for a send: for email the header text (an address as given; a party:id chip by its primary email address, for a party the user may see; a group:id chip by the current members of that contact group who have an email address), for an internal message the party ids (party:id; an address chip by the party with it, match#Addresses; a group:id chip by its members) and the mailboxes (list:id). A group the user may not see is not found. A member with no email address is skipped; a group with none is an error naming it. An entry that cannot be resolved is an error naming it.

Save an email draft (org.moqui.mail.EmailClientServices.save#Draft) from the composer: the identity (fromValue identity:id or account:id of an account the user may send from), the recipient chips, subject and body, with the quoted part of a reply or forward after the body, and for a new draft the message it answers or forwards. Its attachments stay as upload#ComposeAttachment and remove#ComposeAttachment keep them. clientRef, the client's own reference of the draft, makes a retry save the same draft (save#Draft): a draft written offline is saved once, and one sent since comes back unchanged with duplicate true. baseStamp, the draftStamp of the copy the client edited (get#ComposeData, or the last save), keeps a draft saved elsewhere since: nothing is saved, conflict is true and compose is the server's draft as get#ComposeData has it (the client keeps its own as a copy, a new draft with a new clientRef). saveRef, the client's reference of this one save, keeps it sent again after a lost answer from being a conflict with itself. draftStamp is the saved draft's.

parameter.name: strict
parameter.description: A recipient that is not an address is an error (for a send); a draft keeps only those that are

parameter.name: saveRef
parameter.description: The client's reference of this save, so it sent again after a lost answer is not a conflict with itself (save#Draft)

service.description: A draft (ES_DRAFT, or a failed send) of an account the user may send from; an error otherwise.

Files for the composer. For an email draft (emailMessageId) each file is stored as the mail client stores a message's files (dbresource://email/account/message/), and the draft's attachments become its own plus these. Without a draft (an internal message) each file is stored under the user's own folder (dbresource://ironstone/compose/user/) for send#Compose to put on the message. Files over 25 MB are refused.

Attach from Files (design-drawers-commons.md §12 AttachFromFiles): the drive files the user picked (itemList of {driveId, path}), each read through FileServices.get#ResourceInfo as the user (records too), so only a file the user may open is used. For an email draft (emailMessageId) each is copied where the mail client keeps a message's files (dbresource://email/account/message/, the only place save#Draft takes a file from) and added to the draft's attachments; without a draft (an internal message) each is copied under the user's compose folder for send#Compose. A file over maxAttachBytes (25 MB by default) or a folder is not copied: a view link is made for it (FileServices.share#Resource, which needs the user to be allowed to share it) and linkList gives its name and linkPath to put in the message. Each item stands alone: one that fails is named in failedList.
Take a file off an email draft (emailMessageAttachmentId of a draft the user may send from); its file is deleted when the draft keeps it under dbresource://email/.

Send what the composer has. Email (fromValue of a mail account): the draft is saved (strict about recipients), then sent through mantle.party.CommunicationServices.send#EmailDraft with the record chip (which files it on the record once sent, R6) or org.moqui.mail.EmailClientServices.send#Draft without one: at scheduledSendDate, or now after the undo hold of holdSeconds (0 to 300). An internal message (fromValue internal): a reply (parentCommEventId) through reply#CommunicationEvent, which keeps the thread's recipients or its mailbox (replyToSenderOnly answers the sender only) with the added ones; a new message through create#Message, posted in each mailbox chip; the uploaded files (uploadsJson, the user's own) on each message; the record chip linked. The from party is always the user's. archiveThread archives the thread answered (Send and archive). A record the user may not see is refused before anything is sent.
clientRef (email) is the client's own reference of the message, so a client that queued it offline and retries after a lost answer sends it once: when the user's message of that clientRef is no longer a draft (waiting to send, sending, sent, or failed and perhaps gone out), its state comes back (EmailClientServices.get#SendState) with duplicate true and nothing is done. baseStamp and saveRef (email) are as save#ComposeDraft has them: a draft saved elsewhere since the client's copy is not sent (conflict true, with compose, the server's draft). clientRef (internal) makes an internal send once too (ClientSyncServices.claim#ClientRequest, keyed on the send, as one send makes several CommunicationEvents): a retry answers the first send's communicationEventIdList with duplicate true and sends nothing, with the messages' status now. A send that fails keeps no reference, and one whose messages were all taken back since (cancel#ComposeSend) sends again, so a retry or a resend after Undo with the same clientRef sends.

parameter.name: saveRef
parameter.description: The client's reference of this save, so it sent again after a lost answer is not a conflict with itself (save#Draft)

service.description: Undo send. An email waiting in the Outbox (the undo hold or a scheduled send) goes back to Drafts (org.moqui.mail.EmailClientServices.cancel#ScheduledSend); one sent already cannot come back. An internal message the user sent in the last two minutes is withdrawn (its status CeCancelled, so no Inbox lists it).
Discard an email draft of the user's (org.moqui.mail.EmailClientServices.trash#Messages deletes a draft, its files and its copy on an IMAP server). An internal message has no draft on the server.
